result.title: When Fog Becomes a Weapon: Atmospheric Attacks on Visible-Infrared Vision-Language Models
result.comment: 11 pages, 8 figures. Supplementary material (23 pages) is available as an ancillary file
result.summary: Existing adversarial attacks on vision-language models (VLMs) and cross-spectral perception primarily rely on conspicuous, unnatural artifacts, such as vivid adversarial patches or active light beams, that lack physical stealthiness, whereas prior weather attacks largely overlook how one atmosphere simultaneously affects heterogeneous sensors. This raises a key scientific question: can a purely natural, shared fog environment simultaneously disrupt complementary visible and thermal infrared cues without artificial surface modifications? We introduce Fog Manipulation Attack (FMA), a zero-gradient attack that optimizes a common 3D fog state to induce simultaneous semantic failures in visible-infrared VLMs. FMA links shared, depth- and layer-aware atmospheric propagation along scene paths with band-specific imaging physics---visible airlight scattering and thermal path radiance---allowing one realistic fog state to erode both modalities' distinct cues. Experiments show that FMA more than doubles simultaneous failure rates over fidelity-matched random fog, transfers to captioning and VQA, and removes cross-modal compensation, where restoring a clean companion view recovers 64%--74% of lost dual-input VQA answers.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Fog Manipulation Attack（FMA），以零梯度方式优化一个共享的 3D 雾状态，同时破坏可见光与热红外的互补线索，使可见-红外 VLM 在双输入下同时出现语义失败，并迁移到 captioning 与 VQA。
AI.relevance_reason: 文中「跨模态补偿被消除」及恢复干净伴随视图可找回 64%–74% 答案的分析，为视觉证据在 VLM 答案中的实际作用提供了定量诊断线索，可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留与证据使用；但属攻击/鲁棒性研究，未涉及 latent 推理状态本身。
